- [2023/05/29] The Employee Retention Credit (ERC) is a tax credit for businesses to keep employees on payroll during economic hardships like the COVID-19 pandemic.
- [2023/05/29] The ERC is refundable and equals 70% of qualified wages, up to $10,000 per employee per quarter, with a maximum of $28,000 per employee for 2021.
- [2023/05/29] Eligibility for the ERC requires a significant decline in gross receipts (at least 20% in 2021 compared to the same quarter in 2019) or partial/full suspension due to COVID-19 government orders.
- [2023/05/29] Small or medium privately owned businesses can benefit from the ERC to offset payroll costs during economic difficulties.
- [2023/05/29] To claim the ERC, eligible employers must file Form 941 with the IRS.
- [2023/05/29] It is recommended that business owners consult with a tax professional to determine ERC eligibility and credit amount.
